num.note: non-numeric string has no parseable numeric prefix -> clamps to 0

REQUIRED CASE: the string "inf". JS's parseFloat does not recognize the bare word "inf" (only the exact literal "Infinity"), so it already yields NaN -> 0 unaided. ObjC's -[NSString doubleValue] DOES parse "inf" as INFINITY, which is finite-looking to naive code but must be caught by an isfinite() clamp -- this is the exact case Fix 3 exists for; without the clamp ObjC returns INFINITY here where JS returns 0.
the string "nan" parses to a non-finite NaN in both runtimes -> clamps to 0
a JSON null value is not a number -> clamps to 0
key entirely absent from data -> undefined (JS) / nil (ObjC) -> clamps to 0

hotRank.note: zero score clamps to log10(1)=0; sign(0)=0 zeroes the time term too
negative score flips sign(); created_utc is exactly EPOCH+45000 so |time term|=1
created_utc at HOT_EPOCH exactly: time term is 0, hot is pure log10(score)

placement.note: nativeHots sorted descending (for contrast with the next case): the four measured native floors d25/d50/d100/d250 vs the hottest NSFW post anywhere (14452.69, boost 0). It clears d25 and d50 but not d100 or below -- 3 natives outrank it, well off page 1 (25).

REQUIRED CASE: same four native hot values as above but NOT sorted descending -- this is measured reality (r/all's native listing is not hot-ordered) and the entire reason placement is a count of outranking natives, not an insertion index into a sorted list. The expected count is identical to the sorted case because slotFor counts, it does not scan for a sorted position.
same unsorted native set, but boost 0.5 lifts the candidate's effective hot to 14453.19, above all four native floors -- 0 natives outrank it, so it lands at the very top slot.
small unsorted integers, boost 0: candidate is outranked by every native.
tie boundary: comparison is strict '>', so a candidate exactly equal to every native's hot is outranked by none of them.
